explanation:
[EFFECT] Hour of day has a strongly non-monotonic, double-peaked effect. Demand is at its lowest in the very early morning (around 4 a.m., where the contribution is deeply negative), then rises sharply to a morning commuter peak at 8 a.m. It dips slightly through midday, then climbs to the highest point of the day at 5 p.m. (17:00), before falling steadily through the evening back to overnight lows.
[IMPORTANCE] This is by far the most important feature (rank 1), with an importance score nearly three and a half times larger than the next feature — it dominates the model's predictions more than all other features combined.
[RECOMMENDATION] Plan your bike availability and staffing primarily around the hour of the day — ensuring high fleet availability and staff support around the 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. peaks — and secondarily around temperature, scaling up resources on warm days (around 20–31 °C) and scaling back on cold or very rainy days.
